lede: Security as a systems problem. Give me a messy substrate, certificates, malware, domains, threat feeds, models, and the job is the same: decompose it, build the system that makes sense of it, and reason about how it behaves under an adversary.

rows.line: Built the crawl, enrichment and categorization pipeline behind a URL-intelligence platform designed for billions of URLs, then set the platform patterns for a four-person R&D lab and a 30-engineer contract team as Director of Engineering. Initiated NetSTAR Shield and NetSTAR Scout. Now advisor and contract principal engineer.
Threat-intelligence research engineer. Shipped the enterprise threat feeds that became up to $1.3M a year in revenue.
Staffing operations technical lead for bootcamp staff across three systems of record; remote upskilling that cut new-hire cost by $85K a year.
Environmental engineer. ISO 14001 audits, and anomaly detection that took reportable air incidents from 25 a year to 3.
Senior engineering manager for AI security: compliance evidence kept in sync with the system of record, OSCAL-native evidence APIs, and a tiered AI model-security scanner as a durable workflow.
Consulting senior cyber ML architect. Redesigned the analyst workflow and cut triage time 80%; a KQL emulator so queries fail offline before they reach Sentinel.
Web security audits and applied AI: OCR pipelines that automated accounts payable, scoped and delivered end to end.
Speaker: Making OpenSSL Approachable, interactive labs, automation and AI insights. The talk became an open-source program.
Workshop: Can LLMs Outsmart Phishers? A reality check on AI defenses.
Co-presenter and co-author: semantic technologies for cybersecurity education competencies.
Thesis published in the university repository.
Commissioner, Planning and Zoning. Development proposals, zoning changes, public hearings.

areas.name: Architecture at scale
areas.receipt: A crawl and classification pipeline sized for 100M+ URLs: single jobs to 18.7M, about 1M a day. A three-layer dedup and recrawl gate with conditional-write claims as the correctness boundary before any model call. A Go enrichment worker per URL: DNS, RDAP, x509, CRLite revocation.

areas.name: Cost and judgment
areas.receipt: Quarterly compute from $50K to $4K while throughput rose. Measured crawl failures before spending on them: a 500-sample of a 2.1M-URL job was 74% dead DNS and 22% connection errors, so the fix was triage before fetch, not a bigger fleet.

areas.name: AI assurance and governance
areas.receipt: Compliance evidence in bidirectional sync with the GRC system; OSCAL-native APIs; a tiered model-security scanner. The published paper: AI Minimalism, necessity-first security design for intelligent systems.

areas.name: Research that ships
areas.receipt: Graph neural networks for threat categorization and an NL2KQL pipeline, both in preparation; the ISCAP paper on semantic education competencies, published; the thesis.

areas.name: People and partners
areas.receipt: A four-person R&D lab and a 30-engineer contract team on shared platform patterns and evaluation frameworks. A 35-feed aggregator where partners onboard by writing a spec, not code. A seat on a municipal commission.

areas.name: Speaking and writing
areas.receipt: Three conference stages in one year, the Spectral Analysis newsletter, and a public readings list on code as law, security principles, and humans and automation.

emphasis.name: Agentic AI architecture
emphasis.line: Small models as bounded reasoners: the harness owns what they see and the rules that shape answers.

emphasis.name: Threat intelligence systems
emphasis.line: Evidence graphs over pipelines; compound evidence over static rules; unknown is benign until shown otherwise.

emphasis.name: Enterprise AI governance
emphasis.line: Controls as evidence APIs, not spreadsheets; necessity-first design; the model explains, the rulebase decides.
